nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$ satisfying Kolmogorov's cycle condition, fix a reference state $i_0$, and write $w(j)$ for the cycle weight of a state $j$ relative to $i_0$. Then for all states $i, j$ we have $w(i) \cdot P(i, j) = w(j) \cdot P(j, i)$.
nodes.title: Detailed balance for cycle weights

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$ satisfying Kolmogorov's cycle condition, fix a reference state $i_0$, and write $w(j)$ for the cycle weight of a state $j$ relative to $i_0$. If $i, j$ are states with $P(i, j) > 0$, then $w(i) \cdot P(i, j) / P(j, i) = w(j)$.
nodes.title: Cycle weights along a positive transition

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$ satisfying Kolmogorov's cycle condition, and let $i_0, j$ be states. If two paths (finite lists of states) both start at $i_0$, end at $j$, and have positive product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$, then the products of the ratios $P(x, y) / P(y, x)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along the two paths…
nodes.title: Path independence of cycle weight

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$ and fix a reference state $i_0$. The cycle weight of a state $j$ relative to $i_0$ is the product of the ratios $P(x, y) / P(y, x)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along a path (a finite list of states) from $i_0$ to $j$ whose product of transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states is positive, where a ratio with $P(y, x) = 0$…
nodes.title: Cycle weight

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ and let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the same states. If $\pi$ and $P$ satisfy the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$, then $\pi$ is stationary for $P$: $\sum_i \pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j)$ for every state $j$.
nodes.title: Detailed balance implies stationarity

nodes.summary: A probability distribution $\pi$ and a stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ satisfy the detailed balance (reversibility) equations when $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i$ and $j$.
nodes.title: Detailed balance

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$. If a probability distribution $\pi$ satisfies the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$, then $\pi(i) > 0$ for every state $i$.
nodes.title: Detailed balance distributions of irreducible chains are positive

nodes.summary: A probability distribution on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ is a function $\pi$ from the states to $\mathbb{R}$ with $\pi(i) \ge 0$ for every state $i$ and $\sum_i \pi(i) = 1$.
nodes.title: Probability distribution on a finite state space

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$. If $n > 0$ and the $(i, j)$ entry of the $n$-th matrix power $P^n$ is positive, then there is a path from $i$ to $j$ (a finite list of states starting at $i$ and ending at $j$) along which the product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ is positive.
nodes.title: Paths from positive matrix powers

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$. For any two states $i, j$ there is a path from $i$ to $j$ (a finite list of states starting at $i$ and ending at $j$) along which the product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Irreducible chains have positive paths

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ and write $P^n$ for its $n$-th matrix power. Then $P$ is irreducible if for all states $i$ and $j$ there is an $n \ge 1$ with $(P^n)_{ij} > 0$; that is, every state can be reached from every state, itself included, in a positive number of steps.
nodes.title: Irreducible stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: A stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ is reversible if there is a probability distribution $\pi$ on the states that is stationary for $P$ and satisfies the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$.
nodes.title: Reversible stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: A probability distribution $\pi$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ is stationary for a stochastic matrix $P$ on the same states if $\pi P = \pi$, that is, $\sum_i \pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j)$ for every state $j$.
nodes.title: Stationary distribution

nodes.summary: A stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ satisfies Kolmogorov's cycle condition when (1) for all states $x, y$, $P(x, y) > 0$ implies $P(y, x) > 0$; and (2) for every $n \ge 0$ and every loop of states $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$ with $x_n = x_0$ and $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(x_{i+1}, x_i) > 0$, we have $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(x_i, x_{i+1}) = \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} P(x_{i+1}, x_i)$.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov's cycle condition

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an irreducible stochastic matrix on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$. If $P$ is reversible, that is, some probability distribution $\pi$ is stationary for $P$ and satisfies the detailed balance equations $\pi(i) P(i, j) = \pi(j) P(j, i)$ for all states $i, j$, then $P$ satisfies Kolmogorov's cycle condition: (1) for all states $x, y$, $P(x, y) > 0$ implies $P(y, x) > 0$; and (2) for every…
nodes.title: Kolmogorov's cycle theorem, necessity half

nodes.summary: For an irreducible finite Markov chain satisfying the cycle condition, there exists a reversible measure: a distribution satisfying the detailed balance equations (and hence stationary).
nodes.title: Kolmogorov's cycle theorem, sufficiency

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$, and let $l_1, l_2$ be nonempty paths (finite lists of states) such that the last state of $l_1$ is the first state of $l_2$. If the products of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along $l_1$ and along $l_2$ are both positive, then so is the product along the path that follows $l_1$ and then $l_2$ with its first state…
nodes.title: Joining positive paths

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$. For every path (finite list of states), the product of the forward transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along the path is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Path products are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix on the states $\{0, \dots, M\}$, and let $l$ be a path (a finite list of states) whose $i$-th state, counting from $0$, is $l_i$. If the product of the transition probabilities $P(x, y)$ over consecutive states $x, y$ along $l$ is positive, then $P(l_i, l_{i+1}) > 0$ for every $i$ such that $i + 1$ is less than the length of $l$.
nodes.title: Positive path products have positive steps

nodes.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$ and a path of states $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k$, the path product is the real number $\prod_{i=0}^{k-1} P(x_i, x_{i+1})$, the product of the forward transition probabilities along the path. For the empty path and for a path consisting of a single state it is $1$.
nodes.title: Forward path product

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix and let $x_0, \dots, x_k$ and $y_0, \dots, y_l$ be paths of states with $x_k = y_0$. Then the ratio product along the joined path $x_0, \dots, x_k, y_1, \dots, y_l$ equals the ratio product along $x_0, \dots, x_k$ times the ratio product along $y_0, \dots, y_l$.
nodes.title: Ratio product of joined paths

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix, $n$ a natural number and $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n+1}$ states. Then the ratio product along $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n+1}$ equals $\frac{P(c_0, c_1)}{P(c_1, c_0)}$ times the ratio product along $c_1, \dots, c_{n+1}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: First step of the ratio product

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix satisfying Kolmogorov's cycle condition, and let $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$ be a path of states with $n \ge 1$ and $x_0 = x_n$ such that $P(x_{i+1}, x_i) > 0$ for every $i < n$. Then the ratio product along $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The ratio product around a loop is one

nodes.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$, the ratio product along every path of states is nonnegative.
nodes.title: The ratio product is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix, $n$ a natural number and $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_n$ states. Then the ratio product along $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_n$ equals $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \frac{P(c_i, c_{i+1})}{P(c_{i+1}, c_i)}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: The ratio product as a finite product

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix such that $P(x, y) > 0$ implies $P(y, x) > 0$ for all states $x$ and $y$. If the forward path product along a path of states is positive, then the ratio product along that path is positive.
nodes.title: Positive paths have positive ratio product

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a stochastic matrix, $x_0, \dots, x_k$ a path of states and $j$ a state. Then the ratio product along $x_0, \dots, x_k, j$ equals the ratio product along $x_0, \dots, x_k$ times $\frac{P(x_k, j)}{P(j, x_k)}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Ratio product after appending a state

nodes.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$ and a path of states $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k$, the ratio product is the real number $\prod_{i=0}^{k-1} \frac{P(x_i, x_{i+1})}{P(x_{i+1}, x_i)}$, where a quotient with denominator $0$ is taken to be $0$. For the empty path and for a path consisting of a single state it is $1$.
nodes.title: Ratio product along a path

nodes.summary: Every entry of every power of a stochastic matrix is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Powers of a stochastic matrix are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a stochastic matrix $P$ on the finite state space $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-th matrix power $P^n$ is defined by $P^0 = I$, the identity matrix, and $(P^{n+1})_{ij} = \sum_k P(i, k) (P^n)_{kj}$. The entry $(P^n)_{ij}$ is the probability of moving from state $i$ to state $j$ in exactly $n$ steps.
nodes.title: Matrix powers of a stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: For a natural number $M$, a stochastic matrix of size $M + 1$ is a square matrix $P = (P_{ij})$ indexed by the states $\{0, 1, \dots, M\}$, with real entries $P_{ij} \ge 0$ for all states $i, j$, whose rows sum to $1$: $\sum_j P_{ij} = 1$ for every $i$. It is the transition matrix of a Markov chain on these $M + 1$ states.
nodes.title: Stochastic matrix

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
